These blocks contain two segments each, and thus enable a 5-piece assembly (Figure 1).8.Investigators who wish to introduce alterations within the regions spanned by Block 3/4 or Block 6/7 may opt to design a 6- or 7- piece assembly that incorporates the single-segment blocks (Blocks 3, 4, 6 and/or 7).9.The size of the final assembly is calculated by adding the sizes of each of the Blocks (including deletions) and the size of any customized features (e.g., transgene expression cassettes). We recommend the PureLink Midiprep kit for plasmid purification, although other commercially available kits should also be suitable.11.Plasmid stabs obtained from Addgene are in the Stable bacterial strain (NEB). We have found that these plasmids can be routinely propagated in DH5α cells as well.12.The concentration and purity of each plasmid are assessed by spectrophotometry. Note: Addgene now offers the complete set of plasmids as a single toolkit, at a reduced cost. Alternatively, each of the AdenoBuilder plasmids can be acquired separately. Preparation of the plasmid pAd5-B1 typically results in a lower DNA yield compared to the other AdenoBuilder plasmids. This is normal and not usually a problem. If desired, bacteria transformed by pAd5-B1 can be grown in a larger culture volume, as for a low copy plasmid.
CRITICAL: The pJET1.2 vector backbone present in each of the vectors is not integrated into genome assemblies. All size calculations are based on insert sequences only.

steps.title: Obtain required plasmid blocks
steps.instruction: Select the AdenoBuilder blocks that together represent all seven HAd5 genome segments (Blocks 1‑7). For most designs use the consolidated Block 3/4 and Block 6/7 (or their derivatives) to enable a 5‑piece assembly; optionally include individual Blocks 3, 4, 6, 7 for 6‑ or 7‑piece assemblies. Calculate the total genome size by adding the sizes of each block (including any deletions) and any custom transgene cassettes; the final size must be ~34–38 kb. Order the plasmid stabs from Addgene (stable bacterial strain, NEB; can be propagated in DH5α). Purify each plasmid with the PureLink Midiprep kit (or equivalent). Measure DNA concentration and purity by spectrophotometry; the OD260/280 nm ratio must be between 1.7 and 1.9 (NanoDrop recommended). Note that pAd5‑B1 often yields lower DNA amounts; if needed, grow a larger culture volume as for low‑copy plasmids. Remember that the pJET1.2 backbone is not part of the final genome and size calculations use only insert sequences.

steps.title: Digest plasmid mixture with BstBI
steps.instruction: Combine 500 fmol of each purified plasmid in a single 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube (use the NEBiocalculator to convert mass to fmol). Prepare a 100 µL digestion reaction by adding 10 µL of 10× CutSmart buffer, ultrapure distilled water to a total volume of 95 µL, and 5 µL BstBI (20 U/µL). Vortex briefly and pulse‑centrifuge. Incubate at 65 °C for 30 min in a heating block or water bath.

steps.title: Precipitate digested DNA
steps.instruction: To the 100 µL digest add 25 µL of 7.5 M ammonium acetate and 300 µL of 100 % ethanol; vortex briefly. Centrifuge at room temperature for 5 min at maximum speed. Decant the supernatant. Add 500 µL of 70 % ethanol to wash the pellet; centrifuge at maximum speed for 1 min at room temperature. Carefully decant the supernatant and use a pipette to remove residual liquid without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the DNA pellet at room temperature for 15 min (or until no visible ethanol remains). Dissolve the pellet in 5 µL ultrapure distilled water. Incubate the capped tube at 37 °C for 30 min to ensure complete dissolution. Do not over‑dry the pellet with heat or vacuum, as this hampers resuspension.

steps.title: Set up NEBuilder HiFi assembly
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL of 2× NEBuilder HiFi DNA Assembly Master Mix to the resuspended DNA (total DNA amount should be 15–17 µg). Vortex briefly and pulse‑centrifuge to collect liquid at the tube bottom.

steps.title: Incubate and store assembled genome
steps.instruction: Incubate the assembly reaction at 45 °C for 1 h in a heating block or water bath (45 °C gives higher yield of full‑length genomes than the standard 50 °C). After incubation, place the reaction on ice or store at –20 °C until electroporation. No further purification of the assembled DNA is required before electroporation.

description: With the AdenoBuilder system, a researcher can rapidly and efficiently modify any desired genomic region, or multiple regions, in the Human Adenovirus serotype 5 (HAd5) genome and rescue infectious viruses. This protocol describes the specific steps for introducing transgenes in place of the endogenous HAd5 E1 and/or E3 genes, a common goal of many projects. We have also used this protocol to introduce functional point mutations and heterologous epitopes into other parts of the HAd5 genome (Miciak et al., 2018). The AdenoBuilder system is modular, consisting of a series of seven cloned DNA segments that span the 36 kb HAd5 genome (Figure 1). To engineer a new recombinant HAd5 genome, the researcher must first obtain the required plasmid modules, or “blocks”, that compose the desired configuration of the final vector. The first version of the AdenoBuilder system consisted of seven wild type blocks (Blocks 1–7) and three modified blocks designed to accommodate transgenic elements of various sizes (Miciak et al., 2018). Here, the inserts from Blocks 3 and 4 and Blocks 6 and 7 have been consolidated into two plasmids, respectively designated Block 3/4 and Block 6/7. These larger blocks facilitate a highly efficient 5-piece assembly that is suitable for most simple vector designs.Figure 1The expanded AdenoBuilder systemFunctional adenovirus genomes are comprised of seven segments, individually cloned into Blocks 1–7. Several of these segments have been consolidated into larger plasmids, as shown, to facilitate a simplified 5-piece assembly. Blocks that harbor deletions (dotted lines) can be used in combination to accommodate transgenes up to 8 kb in size. GFP expression cassettes, useful for functional titering, are shown in green; endogenous HAd5 viral genes and gene clusters are indicated in red; inverted terminal repeats (ITRs) are shown in orange.
